BiblicalUsage: Once, in Agur's list of things that go well: a greyhound; an he goat also; and a king, against whom there is no rising up. The word is the non-rising, the resistlessness of the king against whom no one can stand, and it closes the proverb with a picture of unchallenged power.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for no rising up carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the picture, that the king walks and no one rises against him.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
